summary: # Fur Generation | Clo 2025.0 Features Deep Dive ## Introduction Hey everyone, my name is Phoebe, and I'm going to show you this really cool new feature called **Fur Strand**. It's going to allow you to see all of your fur in your 3D window. So, let's have some fun while we learn and dive on in! ## Overview of the Fur Strand Feature ### Location of the Feature First off, where is this feature? Well, it’s located where all of our material types are. If I go to my object browser up top here on my right, I can select my fabric. As you all probably know already, when you select a fabric, there will be a yellow highlight in your 3D window telling you which piece is applied. ### Selecting Fabric Here, I have Fabric 2 applied to this piece. I can then go down into my Property Editor, which is right below the Object Browser. If I scroll down a bit underneath Materials, I'll see "Type." This type indicates what type of fabric this is. This is our **fur render-only fabric**. ### Activating Fur Strand Now, if I go to this drop-down, I can see right above "Render Only," there's **Fur Strand**. Selecting this allows you to see the fur in your 3D window. It looks amazing! ## Viewing Options ### Control Options Some things to know: you can control how this is viewed. There are three options on how this is viewed, and we’ll get to where you can view that in a minute. Also, when you switch from Fur Render to Fur Strand, it resets all of your properties, so you will have to reapply them all. ### Presets You can even see here that for "Preset," it now says "Default." Originally, when it was for render, it was set to "Fox." So, I can just easily go to "Fox," and it will show me my Fox fur. ### Compatibility It’s important to note that this feature works in Windows but is not available in Max yet. Apologies for that. However, for all you Windows users, it’s great! Also, this works in your render window, so you do not have to switch to Fur Render to see this in render; you can keep it all as Fur Strand. ## User Settings ### Accessing User Settings Let’s go into our user window. I'm going to go to **User Settings** to see all of the different ways in which you can view your fur in your 3D window. At the very top toolbar, I can go to **Settings**, and from settings, I can go to **User Settings**. ### Fur Strand Shape Here, I'll select User Settings and go into my 3D section. Right below my 3D section is **Fur Strand Shape**. The default is always **Plain** because that helps the software run quickly and also provides a good amount of information for your fur. You can also use **Line** or **Cylinder**. ## Viewing Modes ### Plain Mode To help you understand what you're seeing in **Plain** mode, let's zoom in a bit. In plain mode, you can see the width of the fur, but you can't see the height or depth. You can observe how long it will be, which is useful for visualizing the fur. ### Line Mode Next, let’s go to **Line** mode. This won't give you much information on thickness or width, but it will indicate how long it is. It presents a straight line, showing you the length. This is very useful for editing quickly. ### Cylinder Mode Now, let’s go into **Cylinder** mode. This provides the most information because it represents every single strand as a cylinder. You can see how wide and how long it is. However, this does slow down your software, so if you’re doing a lot of edits, it might become frustrating. ## Rendering Comparison ### Differences Between Fur Strand and Fur Render To show you the difference between Fur Strand and Fur Render Only, I’m going to go to render. There is a bit of a difference between the two when you render them. Fur Strand is much closer to real life than Fur Render was. It gives a more realistic look, showing how the fur falls and reacts to light, making it appear more natural. ## Workflow Ideas ### Example Workflow Now, let's dive into some workflow ideas. Here’s my garment, which is probably how you're all going to work soon because everything you have is rendered, right? Everything is set to Fur Render Only. ### Transitioning to Fur Strand If you switch to Fur Strand, all that information gets changed. You might need to go to **Copy**, then select Fur Strand, and then go down below to paste. This workflow allows you to manage your fabrics efficiently. ### Saving Fabrics Once you’ve made changes, remember to save your fabrics. For example, I’m going to hit **Save**, and then save as **Fur One Strand**. If you did this workflow, you can then select it and hit **Apply**. ## Final Thoughts This workflow is a bit time-consuming but is very straightforward. Thank you all so much for watching! If you have any questions, use the comment section down below. A CLO 3D designer will get back to you. Keep having fun in CLO, and thanks again for watching!
